window: short-window protocol: hard recovery unit (+2400 s) armed before any stop; qwen-inference-health.timer suspended for the window and restored; maintenance lease held; baseline restored and authenticated
first_completed_kvarn_request: first KVarN-profile request on this series to complete end to end (prefill plus generation); the 262144 deep probe never completed

profiler.method: POST /start_profile {output_dir=/cache/prof, activities=[CPU,GPU]} on the pinned v0.5.19 runtime; stopped via /stop_profile
profiler.trace_outcome: lost: chrome-trace export exceeded the container 48g cgroup limit; scheduler process OOM-killed (exit 137, OOMKilled=true) at 2026-09-13T17:48:12Z during serialization
profiler.salvaged_evidence: scheduler batch lines, serving-time Triton compile log, 1 Hz GPU telemetry, completed probe artifacts

engine_progress_during_window.chunk_time_model: deep-probe linear fit t ~= 1.6 + 0.001376*done_tokens predicts 3.0/4.4/5.8 s for chunks 2-4; independent window-1 batch-line deltas 3/5/6 s confirm the same quadratic-in-depth slope
engine_progress_during_window.first_chunk_caveat: chunk-1 scheduler line (88.48 tok/s) is compile-contaminated; pure steady chunk time at done~1K is ~3 s (~340 tok/s), not 27 tok/s

serving_start_triton_jit.window: 17:41:26-17:45:49, first request after readiness, GPU idle, CPU-bound nvcc/ninja/ptxas
serving_start_triton_jit.note: fresh container pays ~4.4 min of serving-time Triton JIT before first steady chunk; upstream log itself recommends pre-compiling during engine init

gpu_telemetry_during_chunks.note: below the deep probe's 271 W median: at shallow depth the 8-query microbatch loop leaves launch gaps that deepen away at scale

implications: The deep probe's '27 tok/s start' was JIT-contaminated; steady shallow-depth prefill is ~300 tok/s and the binding pathology is the depth-linear chunk-time slope 0.001376 s per cached token per 1024-token chunk, now confirmed by two independent windows.

Dense FP8 slope is ~1.9e-5 s/token^2 under the same chunking (1060 tok/s cold at 24K, a~0.5 s): the marginal per-cached-token cost of eager KVarN prefill is ~70x dense FP8, while the fixed per-chunk overhead is only ~3x.

A CPU+GPU torch-profiler capture of this launch-heavy path cannot be exported inside a 48g container; kernel-level attribution requires GPU-only activity capture (see packed-kvarn-2048-kernel-profile.json).
Serving-time Triton JIT (~4.4 min, one kernel 20 s) is a first-request-per-process cost that any cold TTFT benchmark on this path must either absorb in warmup or repair via engine-init precompile.
limitations: No chrome trace survived window 1; kernel attribution comes from the separate window-2 capture.
Throughput figures are scheduler-log lines; profiler CPU overhead and inter-batch idle contaminate them relative to pure forward time.
One request, one depth ramp to 4096 tokens; not capacity or quality evidence.
